---
title: "Customizing a site"
subtitle: "What to do when your site must differ from the WFRC defaults"
toc: true
---

Every WFRC site gets the same defaults from `wfrc-shared.yml`: the theme, the navbar and footer, layout, `freeze: auto` and the "Back to top" link. Most sites need nothing else. When one does, you put **only the differences** in a file called `_site.yml`. This page shows how, with recipes that have been tested.

## The one rule

A value in the shared file **beats the same key in your `_quarto.yml`**. So if the shared file sets a key and you set it again in `_quarto.yml`, your value is silently ignored. A second metadata file listed **after** the shared one beats the shared file. That is what `_site.yml` is:

```yaml
# _quarto.yml
metadata-files:
  - _extensions/WFRCAnalytics/wfrc-brand/wfrc-shared.yml   # org defaults
  - _site.yml                                              # yours: last, so it wins
```

A site made from the starter template already has both lines and an empty `_site.yml`. If you added the extension to an existing project, create `_site.yml` yourself and add the second line.

## Quick start

1. Open `_site.yml`.
2. Delete the `{}` line (it is only there because Quarto rejects a file with no content).
3. Add the keys you need, using the recipes below. Keep the same nesting as in the examples.
4. Run `quarto render`, or check the result with `quarto inspect` (see [Check that it worked](#check-that-it-worked)).

```yaml
# _site.yml: only what this site does differently
execute:
  freeze: false
```

Put in this file **only what differs**. Do not copy the whole shared file or repeat a default: a copied value stops following the org default when it changes.

## Recipes

Each example is a complete `_site.yml`. Combine them by merging the top-level keys (`execute`, `website`, `format`) into one file.

### Always re-run code

The default, `freeze: auto`, re-runs a page only when it changed. Use `false` when results depend on data that lives outside the page, such as model runs, files that change, or the current date.

```yaml
execute:
  freeze: false
```

### Hide the "Back to top" link

```yaml
website:
  back-to-top-navigation: false
```

### Page layout and table of contents

```yaml
format:
  html:
    page-layout: article     # a narrower, centered page (the default is full)
    toc: false               # no table of contents
    toc-expand: 1            # in the contents, open only the current section (the default is 2)
    smooth-scroll: false     # jump instead of animating when a contents link is clicked
    grid:
      sidebar-width: 406px   # a different sidebar width (the default is 350px)
```

### A long menu wraps onto two rows on laptops

The navbar switches to its menu button below 992px. Between about 992px and 1050px, a menu with long labels (for example "Center Buildout Capacity") can wrap onto a second row. This setting is not set by the shared file, so it goes in your own `_quarto.yml`: collapse to the menu button sooner.

```yaml
# _quarto.yml
website:
  navbar:
    collapse-below: xl    # the menu button appears below 1200px instead of 992px
```

### Turn off social-card tags

```yaml
website:
  open-graph: false
```

### Accessibility checking

`axe` reports accessibility problems in the browser console. It is on for every WFRC site on purpose, so only turn it off for a good reason:

```yaml
format:
  html:
    axe: false
```

## What does not need `_site.yml`

`_site.yml` is only for keys that **the shared file sets**. Everything else goes in your own `_quarto.yml`, because nothing is there to override:

- **Yours alone:** `website.title`, `description`, `site-url`, `favicon`, `navbar.left`, `sidebar`, `announcement`, `page-navigation`, and `project.output-dir`, `render`, `resources`.
- **Not set by the shared file:** `jupyter`, `engine`, `execute.echo`, `warning`, `message`, `format.html.css`, `number-sections`, `code-fold`, `code-tools`, `code-link`, `html-math-method`, `lightbox`, `title-block-banner`.

The keys the shared file **does** set, and so the only ones you ever override in `_site.yml`:

| Area | Keys |
|---|---|
| Website | `twitter-card`, `open-graph`, `cookie-consent`, `back-to-top-navigation`, `navbar.logo-alt`, `navbar.right` (Follow Us), `navbar.tools` (GitHub), `page-footer` |
| HTML format | `theme`, `highlight-style`, `respect-user-color-scheme`, `link-external-newwindow`, `include-after-body`, `axe`, `page-layout`, `toc`, `toc-expand`, `smooth-scroll`, `grid` |
| Execution | `execute.freeze` |
| Other | `citation` |
| Project | `project.post-render` (fills in the GitHub menu) |

## What you cannot do

- **Remove a menu or the footer.** Lists (navbar items, tools, footer links) **append** across files, so `_site.yml` can add items but not take away the "Follow Us" menu, the GitHub menu or the footer links. A site that truly needs a different footer must keep a local copy of the shared file.
- **Change the theme.** Do not override `theme` or `highlight-style`. Colors and fonts come from `brand.yml`; see the [brand guide](brand-guide.qmd).
- **Add your own GitHub menu.** It points at your repository by itself. A second one (`navbar.tools` with GitHub, or `repo-url` with `repo-actions`) would appear twice.
- **Use `format: wfrc-brand-html` in a website.** It conflicts with the shared file's `format.html` and Quarto fails when it renders each page twice. Websites use plain `format: html`.

## For one page or one folder

You do not always need a site-wide change. These beat the shared file too:

- **One page:** put it in that page's front matter.

  ```yaml
  ---
  title: "Live model results"
  execute:
    freeze: false
  ---
  ```

- **One folder:** put a `_metadata.yml` in the folder. It applies to the pages in that folder only, not to its subfolders.

  ```yaml
  # reports/_metadata.yml
  execute:
    freeze: false
  ```

Site-wide settings such as `website.*` keys cannot be changed this way; use `_site.yml` for those.

## Check that it worked

Print the settings Quarto will actually use for a page:

```bash
quarto inspect reports/model.qmd
```

Look under `formats` then `html`: `execute.freeze`, and in `metadata` the keys you changed (`page-layout`, `toc-expand`, `grid`). For a `website.*` key, render and look at the page (the "Back to top" link, the social tags in the page source).

If your setting seems ignored:

- Is it in `_quarto.yml` and also set by the shared file? Move it to `_site.yml`.
- Is `_site.yml` listed **after** the shared file in `metadata-files`? Order matters: the later file wins.
- Is the indentation right? `format`, `html` and the key must each be nested two spaces under the one above.
- Did you leave the `{}` line in? Delete it once the file has real keys, or Quarto reports that it cannot read the file.
- Did Quarto cache an old render? Remove the `.quarto` folder and render again.
